That this has been pending over a month without any comments already shows this project is in need of additional help in maintenance.

+1 because jagpal is already maintaining https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt and IMO it's been going well so far.

> That this has been pending over a month without any comments already shows this project is in need of additional help in maintenance.

At the end of the day, this decision needs to come from developers.  The fact that nobody replied for a month might just be due to developers not having a strong opinion here?  I'm going to take that stance, because the alternative (nobody cares enough about these interfaces or Jagpal maintaining them) doesn't sound great to me and would imply we've done something wrong.

FWIW, I keep a prioritized list of reviews, and if nobody has reviewed something, it falls lower on the list for me personally.   Keep in mind, there are currently listed 4 top level maintainers in dbus-sensors (was 5 until recently), but most of them are absent.  Thats something we need to clear up at TOF level, but arguably this new maintainer decision should've been driven by consensus and not "does Ed think this is a good idea" which seems to be what's implied.

Jagpal, I see you've only signed up to maintain the two applications you had a hand in.  This is fine, but PLEASE do not check in generic reactor components into the individual handlers just because you have the power.  I'd really like you to get to the point where you're comfortable navigating the common code as well, and this is an excellent first step.

I'll note that of the 4 maintainers listed, at least 2 people failed to update their new emails, which I assume implicitly means they don't want to maintain anymore.  This is something to be taken up, and is likely why they also haven't replied to this review.

Overall, I'm in support.  Lets get the files cleaned up, and give a little time now that some people have reviewed it in case anyone else wants to chime in and give their support, then this LGTM.

> do not check in generic reactor components into the individual handlers

What do you mean by mean by this? Can you be more specific?

> The fact that nobody replied for a month might just be due to developers not having a strong opinion here?

Maybe we should CC a bunch more people when the folder restructuring goes through and we get to vote on jagpal also helping out with asio common code.

Otherwise people might miss these patches entirely.

Anyways we are making good progress here and gathered 3 votes so resolving this comment.

Lets try to keep the common code common, and ideally not have the "asio" and "coroutines" versions of every generic object.  Ideally we'd have a pattern that lets us do common code, and just have simple methods with wrappers/ifdefs/templates/whatever around the IO portions.

> Lets try to keep the common code common, and ideally not have the "asio" and "coroutines" versions of every generic object.  Ideally we'd have a pattern that lets us do common code, and just have simple methods with wrappers/ifdefs/templates/whatever around the IO portions.


Its a good northstar but we also need to keep in mind that asio and couroutines are 2 different coding patterns. asio is callback based and couroutines follows continuous code pattern with co_await suspension points. Hence, we need to be careful about how we abstract them. Having said that, this is a topic for future discussion when we will evaluate this refactoring, so i am marking this as resolved.

Selectively calling out files like this isn't something I really want to support.  Either you support the common code AS A WHOLE, or you don't.  Simple as that.  These files very likely will be renamed/split/combined, and I don't really want to be changing the owners file every time that happens.

If there's some common theme on these files that we can codify in the folder structure, I'm happy to support that, but these kind of seem like a listing of "files Jagpal wrote" which I don't think we want to maintain.

lets get this file list removed for now so we can get this approved in concept, and see if we can restructure a little bit to make this not a list of files.  (i'm open to options on what that looks like, and there's some discussion already on alexanders review).

@paligill@gmail.com Is there some refactoring we can do to make it clear which parts use ASIO and which parts use sdbusplus::async?  I think that would make it clearing than an arbitrary list of files.

I agree we can move the files into folders with some defined topics. That will also help to create some buckets in terms of general code readability/maintainability. Based on above comment from Ed, I just noticed that there is already an open discussion between Alexander and Ed here https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/83895/comments/67bc863d_62f5a62b. So, will reply there and will also try to help with some of that effort.

For this PR, 
- I will add the OWNERS file into src/leakdetector and src/cable-monitor to make it consistent as asked by Ed here https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/82895/comment/b6881039_06230f3b/.
- I will drop the partial_regex for individual files at the moment and will add the OWNERS for named folders for common code when that gets merged.
 

PS: Having said this i am open to help with maintaining common code, no specific reservation to these set of files.

> So, will reply there and will also try to help with some of that effort.

I appreciate it.

> Having said this i am open to help with maintaining common code, no specific reservation to these set of files.

I REALLY appreciate this.

I am marking this as resolved and let's continue further discussion on this topic in https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/83895, where i had provided feedback to Alexander on organizing the folder structure.

Please take a look at

src/mctp/OWNERS

we seem to be going the "file per folder" path at the moment.  I don't have a strong opinion either way aside from I'd like us to remain consistent, and that's the pattern we have.
Acknowledged
Maybe we can consider going ahead with this patch for now since the common code restructuring does not look like it's going to merge very soon.
After the fact, but to indicate support.
